purpose: Dense Basic Five evaluation (ADE20K, NYUv2) with a fully frozen pretrained backbone read by a multi-layer DPT probe, to measure how much dense information a stronger frozen readout recovers beyond the single-layer 1x1 probe.

optimization_baselines.probe: BASIC5_ATTENTIVE_v1 block of the task, with the learning rate of the reference DPT probe (Geosubprobe probe_lr)

provenance.written: 2026-11-19, after the runs, from the code and the run records
provenance.reference_implementation: DPT probe of Probe3D (El Banani et al., CVPR 2024) as released in Geosubprobe (evals/models/probes.py, class DPT; config depth_dpt: hidden_dim 512, kernel 3; configs/optimizer/*_epoch.yaml: probe_lr 5e-4 at batch_size 8)
provenance.note: The runs read their task definitions and optimizer blocks from BASIC5_{LINEAR,ATTENTIVE}_v1.json and the DPT constants from the code. This file documents those runs; it was not an input to them.

design_principle: Preserve the dataset, split, input geometry, epoch count, loss, and metric of BASIC5_FAIR_v1. Keep the backbone fully frozen and replace the single-layer 1x1 head by a DPT probe that reads four evenly spaced intermediate blocks. Use the BASIC5_ATTENTIVE_v1 optimizer block of the task with the learning rate of the reference DPT probe.

not_applicable.coco: detection keeps the BASIC5_FAIR_v1 feature pyramid and Faster R-CNN

global_rules.pretrained_weights: Use the released pretrained checkpoint as-is; no intermediate adaptation or task-specific pretraining.
not_trainable: backbone normalization affine parameters and running statistics

taps.rule: blocks ceil(k L / 4) - 1 for k = 1..4 (0-based; L = number of transformer blocks), the evenly spaced choice of DPT for ViT-L ([5, 11, 17, 23])
taps.exception: VGGT-Omega uses the four aggregator layers its own DPT heads read (4, 11, 17, 23); the rule would give 5 in place of 4. The adapter checks that the cached set equals these layers.
taps.tensor: Block output tokens with non-spatial special tokens removed, reshaped to the patch grid in raster order. RAEv2-K7 uses the official DINOv3 get_intermediate_layers(norm=True) of its DINOv3-L encoder. VGGT-Omega uses its cached aggregator outputs (frame and global tokens concatenated). Cosmos 3 Super taps its vision-tower blocks before the merger (1152-d, 14x14), whereas its LP/LoRA feature is the 5120-d merger output at 7x7.
taps.feature_cache: Not used; taps are extracted online under no_grad.

dpt_probe.topology: per tap: LayerNorm over channels -> 1x1 Conv C -> 512 -> x2 bilinear upsampling (align_corners=true); fusion from the deepest tap to the shallowest: fuse4(tap4); fuse3(tap3, .); fuse2(tap2, .); fuse1(tap1, .), each fusion = ResidualConvUnit(tap) + previous, then ResidualConvUnit; x4 bilinear upsampling (align_corners=true); Conv3x3 512->512, ReLU, Conv3x3 512->out; bilinear resize to the target size (align_corners=false)
dpt_probe.residual_conv_unit: Conv3x3 -> ReLU -> Conv3x3 -> ReLU, plus identity

outputs.nyuv2: 1 channel, depth = softplus(x) + 1e-3 (the BASIC5_FAIR_v1 positive parameterization)

changes_from_reference: LayerNorm over channels on each tap before its projection, because the six backbones expose raw block outputs whose scales differ by orders of magnitude (pre-norm residual streams; Cosmos 3 Super block outputs about 1e3).
The reference's final fixed x2 upsampling is replaced by a bilinear resize to the target size (align_corners=false), as in the Unified LP readout.
dpt_probe.same_grid_note: All four taps share one patch grid (14x14 at 224 px), so the fusion stages do not upsample between taps.

global_rules.hyperparameter_policy: One recipe per task, applied unchanged to all six models. No model-specific learning rate, tap selection (beyond the VGGT-Omega exception above), or probe width.
global_rules.precision: bfloat16 backbone weights and bfloat16 autocast; probe parameters, loss, and metrics in float32.

lr_group_rules.no_decay: 1-D parameters (biases, LayerNorm affine) and parameters whose name contains 'norm'
lr_group_rules.schedule_unit: The learning rate advances once per optimizer step over epochs x steps_per_epoch steps.

input.train: random rescale by [0.5, 2.0] (bicubic, each side at least 224 px), random 224x224 crop, random horizontal flip p=0.5
input.evaluation: image resized to 224x224 (bicubic), label resized to 224x224 (nearest)
input.normalization: the pretrained backbone's published input normalization

ade20k.feature_and_pooling: Four frozen taps (global_rules.taps) read by the DPT probe; logits resized to the label size.
ade20k.head: DPT probe with 150 outputs
ade20k.augmentation: Same geometry as BASIC5_FAIR_v1; no photometric augmentation.

metrics.primary: mean IoU over 150 classes on the 2,000 validation images, final epoch

ade20k.minimal_deviation_note: Split, 20 epochs, input, loss, and metric stay fixed; the 1x1 Conv on one layer is replaced by the DPT probe on four frozen layers.

nyuv2.split: official Eigen-style 795 train / 654 test from labeled.mat and splits.mat

input.orientation: Images and depth maps read in their true 480x640 orientation (the basic5 loader transposed them).
input.train: image resized to 224x224 (bicubic), depth resized to 224x224 (bilinear), random horizontal flip p=0.5
input.evaluation: the same deterministic 224x224 resize without flip
input.normalization: the pretrained backbone's published input normalization

nyuv2.feature_and_pooling: Four frozen taps (global_rules.taps) read by the DPT probe; depth resized to the target size.
nyuv2.head: DPT probe with one output channel, depth = softplus(x) + 1e-3
nyuv2.loss: scale-invariant log-depth loss on valid pixels, lambda = 0.5: mean(d^2) - 0.5 * mean(d)^2 with d = log(pred) - log(gt)

metrics.evaluation_mask: valid pixels with 0.1 < depth < 10 m; predictions clamped to [0.1, 10]
metrics.primary_in_record: RMSE in meters after per-image median scale alignment (field rmse)
metrics.paper_metric: RMSE in meters without alignment (field rmse_unaligned), as defined in the paper's evaluation appendix

nyuv2.minimal_deviation_note: Split, mask and range, 30 epochs, input, loss, and metrics stay fixed; the 1x1 depth head on one layer is replaced by the DPT probe on four frozen layers.

reporting.checkpoint_rule: Use the final scheduled epoch; no selection on the reported validation/test split.
reporting.seed_aggregation: Report mean and sample standard deviation (ddof = 1) over seeds 0, 1, and 2; retain every per-seed result.
required_metadata: tap blocks and tap tensor shapes
epochs, batch, realized learning rate and its source, steps per epoch, total steps
code sha256, PBS job id, host, GPU, torch and python versions
reporting.validity_rule: A cell counts only with COMPLETED_VALID.json, the recipe's epoch count reached, steps_per_epoch x epochs = total steps, and evaluation on the full split.
reporting.failure_rule: Do not tune a single failing model. Apply a protocol-wide fix to every model, increment the version, and disclose it.

version_history.recipe: The DPT probe trained at the BASIC5_ATTENTIVE_v1 learning rate (1e-3 at batch 8).
version_history.outcome: The training loss rose after warm-up and ended above the 1x1 linear probe's training loss for DINOv3-7B, V-JEPA 2.1, and RAEv2 on ADE20K, the three models where DPT scored below LP; seed spread was 3-5x that of LP and LoRA. Cells kept under DPT/ as a record.

version_history.change: The probe trains at the learning rate of the reference DPT probe it copies (5e-4 at batch 8, linearly scaled); everything else unchanged. Applied to all six models and both tasks. The learning rate comes from the reference implementation, not from the reported split.

deviations_from_unified_code: NYUv2 frames are read upright (the basic5 loader transposed them).
The learning-rate schedule advances per optimizer step.
